On Windows, open Command Prompt and run: copy /b file_part1+file_part2+file_part3 whole.ext. On Linux or macOS, run: cat file_part* > whole.ext. Replace the names with your actual part names, in numeric order.

split-files.formula:
Number of parts = ceil(file size in bytes / chunk size in bytes).
Size of each full part = chunk size in bytes.
Size of the last part = file size - (parts - 1) x chunk size.
Example: 52,428,800 bytes / 10,485,760 bytes = 5 parts.
howTo: Click the file button and choose the file you want to split.
Pick "By chunk size" and enter the megabytes per part, or "By number of parts" and enter how many parts you want.
The tool instantly shows the file size, the number of parts, and the size of each part.
Download parts one by one, or use "Download all parts" to save them together.
Move or share the parts, then rejoin them in order on the other side to restore the original file.
keyFacts: Splitting cuts a file into exact byte ranges — no compression, no format change, no data loss.
Two ways to split: by chunk size (every part is at most N MB) or by number of parts (parts are as equal as possible).
Part names get a _part1, _part2 suffix before the file extension so they sort in order.
The last part is usually smaller — it holds whatever bytes are left over.
To rejoin, concatenate the parts in numeric order (Windows: copy /b part1+part2 whole; Linux/macOS: cat part* > whole).

split-files.quickAnswer: Pick a file, choose a chunk size (for example 10 MB) or a number of parts (for example 4), and download each part separately. A 50 MB file split into 10 MB chunks gives you 5 parts named file_part1 to file_part5. Parts are exact byte slices, so nothing is changed or compressed — rejoin them in order to restore the original.

split-files.workedExample:
File: backup.zip, 50 MB (52,428,800 bytes). Chunk size: 10 MB (10,485,760 bytes).
1. Parts = 52,428,800 / 10,485,760 = 5.
2. Parts 1 to 4 are each 10,485,760 bytes (10 MB).
3. Part 5 = 52,428,800 - (4 x 10,485,760) = 52,428,800 - 41,943,040 = 10,485,760 bytes (10 MB).
4. You download backup_part1.zip to backup_part5.zip and rejoin them in order to get the original 50 MB file back.
